newsitem.title: CHINA: China hails progress in firing up frigid pandas.
newsitem.headline: China hails progress in firing up frigid pandas.

text.p: China on Wednesday claimed progress in the fight to convince its famously frigid female pandas that sex is more fun than munching fresh bamboo shoots.

Scientists had found that hormone supplements could cause sexual excitement in female pandas that normally looked on males with little more than contempt, a discovery that could help save the endangered species, the official Xinhua news agency said.

"Most female giant pandas cannot enter into periods of sexual excitement easily or at least not obviously so during the mating season," it quoted Professor Chen Dayuan of the Institute of Zoology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences as saying.
Only 10 percent of giant pandas could mate naturally and their lack of fecundity was the main reason for their endangered status, Xinhua said.
Scientists had found that gonadotropins, hormones that support the growth of reproductive cells, determined sexual excitement in female pandas, it said.

"To get to the root of the problem, the research group has experimented with giving supplemental hormones to the female giant panda, so as to stimulate her into a period of sexual excitement and help her to produce eggs," it said.

"When the female giant panda produces a sufficient secretion of gonadotropins, she will attain a state of sexual excitement; when inadequate, she will show indifference to the male even in the mating season," it quoted Chen as saying.

Supplemental hormones had helped pandas get pregnant and give birth as long ago as 1989, it said, adding that a research paper by Chen's team had been published in a recent Chinese scientific journal.
